meta.subtitle: Sanitized Windows endpoint exports drive this exercise. No VM is required: trainees investigate a downloaded evidence pack built from realistic Sysmon, PowerShell, Security, Task Scheduler, proxy, and DNS telemetry.
meta.workspace_note: Evidence-pack workflow using sanitized Windows Server and workstation exports instead of a live VM.
meta.services_copy: Query shell, IOC evidence board, timeline review, host logs, and local run scoring.
meta.target_note: Credential dumping via procdump.exe remains the clearest escalation clue in the case file.
meta.ioc_note: Four seeded indicators came from sanitized host, email, DNS, and proxy exports.

alerts.title: Suspicious outbound DNS queries
alerts.description: WS-FINANCE-03 queried dns-tunnel.malware.io 1,200 times per minute.

alerts.title: Credential dump detected (LSASS)
alerts.description: procdump.exe accessed lsass.exe on WS-FINANCE-03 with memory-read permissions.

alerts.title: New scheduled task created
alerts.description: WindowsUpdate_svc was registered with SYSTEM privileges and an AtLogon trigger.

queries.label: Credential Dumping
queries.search:
ResponseGridLogs
| where host == "WS-FINANCE-03" and ("procdump.exe" or "dns-tunnel.malware.io")
| summarize earliest = min(timestamp), latest = max(timestamp) by host, process_name, parent_process, user, dest_domain, task_name

09:14:25 powershell.exe WINWORD.EXE finance-user dns-tunnel.malware.io -
09:31:42 procdump.exe cmd.exe finance-user - -
09:45:14 schtasks.exe cmd.exe SYSTEM - WindowsUpdate_svc

correlation: phishing > PowerShell > LSASS dump > scheduled task persistence
queries.raw:
09:31:42 WS-FINANCE-03 sysmon:process Image=C:\Tools\procdump.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe GrantedAccess=0x1010
09:45:14 WS-FINANCE-03 windows:taskscheduler TaskName=WindowsUpdate_svc Author=SYSTEM Trigger=AtLogon
09:18:11 proxy-01 web:proxy dest_ip=203.0.113.42 sni=update-win365.net action=allowed
queries.timeline:
09:12 phishing email delivered
09:14 macro execution and PowerShell launcher

queries.label: Initial Access
queries.search:
ResponseGridLogs
| where host == "WS-FINANCE-03" and ("phish-invoice.docm" or "powershell.exe")
| project timestamp, process_name, parent_process, user, file_name, command_line

09:14:22 WINWORD.EXE explorer.exe finance-user phish-invoice.docm macro enabled
09:14:25 powershell.exe WINWORD.EXE finance-user - encoded command executed

launch chain confirms phishing-led initial access.
queries.raw:
09:14:25 WS-FINANCE-03 powershell:operational ParentImage=WINWORD.EXE CommandLine=powershell.exe -enc SQBFAFgA...
09:12:03 mail-gw-01 o365:message_trace sender=billing@invoice-sync.net subject="Invoice review" attachment=phish-invoice.docm
queries.timeline:
09:12 email delivered
09:14 document opened
09:14 macro launched PowerShell
queries.status: Initial access query completed. Document-to-PowerShell chain confirmed.

queries.label: Persistence
queries.search:
ResponseGridLogs
| where host == "WS-FINANCE-03" and ("WindowsUpdate_svc" or "schtasks.exe")
| project timestamp, process_name, parent_process, user, task_name, trigger

09:45:14 schtasks.exe cmd.exe SYSTEM WindowsUpdate_svc AtLogon
09:45:17 taskeng.exe services.exe SYSTEM WindowsUpdate_svc Registered

persistence is active at user logon with SYSTEM privileges.
queries.raw:
09:45:14 WS-FINANCE-03 windows:taskscheduler TaskName=WindowsUpdate_svc Trigger=AtLogon Author=SYSTEM
09:45:18 WS-FINANCE-03 security EventID=4698 TaskName=WindowsUpdate_svc SubjectUserName=SYSTEM
queries.timeline:
09:31 credential access
09:45 scheduled task created
09:46 persistence checkpoint reached
queries.status: Persistence query completed. Scheduled task remains the active foothold.

evidence.summary: High-volume DNS tunneling aligned with beaconing from the compromised workstation.
evidence.note: Pivot to proxy and DNS telemetry. This IOC is the strongest command-and-control signal in the run.

evidence.summary: Outbound TLS sessions from the workstation and proxy tier resolve to the active attacker node.
evidence.note: Use this IOC for network block simulation and for validating proxy-enforced containment.

evidence.summary: Credential dumping utility executed against LSASS with memory-read permissions.
evidence.note: This artifact should drive both the credential-access finding and the host containment recommendation.

evidence.summary: Macro-enabled document delivered through phishing and linked to the first PowerShell execution.
evidence.note: Keep this selected during stakeholder demos to show clear mapping from phishing artifact to host compromise.

timeline.desc: Phishing email received by finance-user@corp.local with a macro-enabled attachment.
User opens phish-invoice.docm and the macro launches a PowerShell dropper.
Reverse shell established from WS-FINANCE-03 to 203.0.113.42:443.
Credentials dumped from lsass.exe using procdump.exe.
Persistence established via scheduled task WindowsUpdate_svc.

logs.event: Message delivered from billing@invoice-sync.net with attachment phish-invoice.docm
Encoded command executed from WINWORD.EXE child process
procdump.exe opened lsass.exe with PROCESS_VM_READ access

base.message: Scenario B loaded from a sanitized Windows endpoint evidence pack.
Start with the email and PowerShell chain to lock down initial access.
LSASS access is confirmed. Preserve that evidence before cleanup.
The suspicious domain appears in both DNS and proxy exports.
